overview: Flow Traders is a leading global electronic liquidity provider and market maker, specializing in Exchange Traded Products (ETPs) and operating across equities, fixed income, FX, commodities, and digital assets. Founded in 2004 and listed on Euronext Amsterdam, the firm trades exclusively from its own capital (no client AuM) across 180+ exchanges and trading venues, serving 2,000+ institutional counterparties including banks, asset managers, pension funds, and hedge funds. The company operates three main trading hubs in Amsterdam, New York, and Hong Kong, with branch offices in London, Paris, Singapore, Chicago, Milan, Shanghai, and Cluj-Napoca.

business_model.summary: Flow Traders earns Net Trading Income (NTI) by capturing the bid-ask spread on continuous two-way price quotes across ETPs and other asset classes. The firm trades delta-neutral, meaning it hedges positions to remain market-direction agnostic; revenue is driven by trading volumes, market volatility, and the firm's ability to price instruments competitively. Revenue is transactional and volume/volatility-dependent rather than recurring — NTI fluctuates materially with market conditions. The firm does not provide services to clients and does not manage client assets; it acts exclusively as principal.

revenue_streams.name: Digital Assets (crypto spot, derivatives, crypto ETPs)

business_model.customer_type: B2B institutional — banks, asset managers, pension funds, insurance companies, hedge funds, family offices. Over 2,000 institutional counterparties globally. No retail clients; no client AuM.
business_model.geographic_mix: Europe 59% of NTI (FY2024: €313m), Asia 17% (FY2024: €81m, growing strongly), Americas 16% (FY2024: €73m). In FY2025, Asia grew to €122m (25% of NTI), Europe €159m (58%), Americas €41m (15%). Asia is the fastest-growing region.

competitive_position.market_position: Global leader in European ETP market making (both on-exchange and off-exchange RFQ). Leading position in crypto ETP market making in Europe. Flow Traders ETP value traded was €1,940bn in FY2025 against a global market of €68,915bn — approximately 2.8% of global ETP volumes and an estimated 10-15% of European ETP volumes. US market remains dominated by Citadel Securities and Jane Street; Flow Traders Americas NTI is only ~15-16% of total despite the US representing 85-90% of global ETP volumes.

moat_factors.description: Fully in-house developed, high-performance automated trading platform with over 40% of workforce in technology roles. The tech stack underpins ultra-low-latency pricing, risk management, and multi-asset hedging at scale. Difficult and costly for new entrants to replicate, with decades of optimization embedded in the codebase.

moat_factors.factor: Global regulatory licenses and exchange memberships
moat_factors.description: Access to 180+ exchanges and trading venues globally, with regulated entities in the Netherlands, US, and Hong Kong. Obtaining and maintaining memberships and regulatory approvals across this many venues is a significant barrier to entry.

2,000+ institutional counterparties on the off-exchange RFQ network. Relationships built over 20 years create deep bilateral flow visibility. New entrants cannot easily replicate this breadth of buy-side relationships or the trust required for large-block off-exchange trading.

moat_factors.factor: First-mover advantage in European ETPs and crypto ETPs
moat_factors.description: Flow Traders has been trading European ETPs since 2004 and entered digital assets in 2017, creating deep product expertise and embedded relationships with ETP issuers. Designated as the #1 crypto ETP market maker in Europe. However, well-funded competitors are increasingly active in these markets.

Trading Capital grew to €1,044m at end FY2025 (up 35% YoY), driven by the Trading Capital Expansion Plan and the $200m private credit facility. More capital enables larger positions, better pricing, and entry into new asset classes. However, the capital base remains significantly smaller than private mega-competitors.

moat_factors.factor: Digital assets and RWA ecosystem positioning
moat_factors.description: Connected to 20+ crypto trading venues, provides liquidity in 200+ cryptocurrencies. AllUnity (JV with DWS and Galaxy) launched a MiCAR-compliant EUR stablecoin (EURAU) in July 2025, with Deutsche Borse onboarding for institutional custody. Partnership with Dinari for 24/7 tokenized US equity trading (Q1 2026 launch). Viewed as a leader in bridging TradFi and DeFi, particularly in Europe.

weaknesses: Revenue is heavily dependent on market volatility and trading volumes — periods of low volatility significantly compress NTI; 3Q25 EBITDA margin fell to 24% in a low-volatility environment versus 52% in high-vol 4Q24
Relative scale disadvantage versus private peers: Citadel Securities earned ~$9.7bn in 2024 and Jane Street captured ~10% of US equity market, versus Flow Traders' €486m NTI in FY2025

Americas market remains underpenetrated — the US is 85-90% of global ETP volumes, yet Flow Traders Americas NTI was only 15-16% of total in FY2024-FY2025, highlighting the difficulty of breaking into the US market against entrenched domestic players
Public company disclosure requirements provide competitors with visibility into strategies, performance, and capital levels that private competitors can keep confidential
Dividend suspended since 2Q24 as capital is retained for the Trading Capital Expansion Plan, reducing appeal for income-seeking investors with no clarity on resumption timing

growth_drivers: Global ETP AuM expected to grow from $14.8tn (end 2024) to $25tn by 2030 — a 2.5x increase — directly expanding the addressable trading volume for Flow Traders' core business. Global ETP inflows were a record $1.88tn in 2024 and $898bn in just H1 2025.

Crypto and digital asset expansion: spot Bitcoin ETF launches in the US in January 2024 drove 826% growth in crypto ETP AuM in one year. Flow Traders is the #1 crypto ETP market maker in Europe. Further crypto ETP launches (Ethereum, Solana) and growing institutional adoption represent a large incremental opportunity.

Fixed income electronification: 50% of Euro IG credit already executed electronically (rising to 75% on a ticket-count basis), with fixed income ETF AuM set to triple from $2tn to $6tn by 2030. Flow Traders is investing in model pricing, portfolio trading, and direct credit market making to capture this structural shift.

Asia and China expansion: Asia NTI grew from €36.8m (FY2023) to €81.5m (FY2024) to €122m (FY2025) — more than 3x in two years. Flow Traders launched active trading in China markets in H2 2025 — described by CEO Spitz as 'an attractive growth segment aligned with our core ETP strength.' The Asian ETP market remains fragmented and underpenetrated.

Real-world asset (RWA) tokenization: Flow Traders views tokenization as the 'new ETP moment'. AllUnity EUR stablecoin launched July 2025; Deutsche Borse onboarded EURAU via Clearstream; Dinari partnership enables 24/7 trading of 200+ tokenized US equities from Q1 2026. RWA tokenization could reach $30tn by 2030.

Trading Capital Expansion Plan: $200m private credit facility and $75m revolving credit facility secured in October 2025 enables deployment of more capital across regions and asset classes. Trading Capital grew 35% to €1,044m in FY2025, with Return on Average Trading Capital of 53%. Each incremental euro of trading capital deployed generates NTI with limited additional fixed cost.

AI and deep learning: new CTO Owain Lloyd is deploying AI-supported analytics and a dedicated Deep Learning initiative applied to trading strategies, targeting improvements in pricing competency, execution efficiency, and quantitative mid/short-term trading capabilities.

24/7 market infrastructure: the shift toward continuous trading across TradFi and DeFi plays to Flow Traders' multi-timezone, multi-venue market-making infrastructure. The company expects to fully support 24/7 trading for all partners in TradFi and DeFi soon.

business.description: Flow Traders' NTI is primarily driven by market volatility and trading volumes. In low-volatility periods, EBITDA margins collapse: 3Q25 EBITDA margin was 24% with a VIX of 16.0, versus 52% in 4Q24 with a VIX of 17.3. FY2023 NTI was only €300m in a low-vol environment. This makes earnings inherently lumpy and highly sensitive to macro conditions outside management's control.

Citadel Securities, Jane Street, Optiver, and others are private firms with no public reporting constraints, larger capital bases, and aggressive global expansion. Citadel Securities earned ~$9.7bn in 2024; Jane Street captured ~10% of US equity market volume. These firms are increasingly active in Flow Traders' European ETP stronghold and digital assets. Optiver opened a Manhattan office in August 2025 specifically to challenge Citadel and Jane Street. Virtu and Optiver signed a US options alliance in January 2026. Competitive intensity is meaningfully rising.

The US is 85-90% of global ETP volumes but only 15-16% of Flow Traders' NTI. Despite years of investment, breaking into the entrenched US market-making landscape remains structurally challenging, limiting full monetization of global ETP growth.

Flow Traders' competitive edge depends on a small, highly skilled team of traders, quants, and software engineers who are in extreme demand. Retention of top talent — particularly in the face of competition from private firms offering larger compensation packages without public scrutiny — is an ongoing strategic risk.

financial.description: NTI swings dramatically with market conditions: FY2021 NTI was €1.07bn; FY2022 was €472m; FY2023 was €300m; FY2024 was €468m; FY2025 was €486m. Within a single year, quarterly NTI ranged from €78m (3Q25) to €154m (4Q24) — nearly a 2x swing. This inherent unpredictability makes valuation and forecasting difficult and contributes to a valuation discount.

The $200m private credit facility (SOFR + 5%, 6-year term) and $75m revolving facility add leverage that did not exist before. Interest expenses were €4.4m in FY2025, rising to approximately €12-15m annualized in FY2026. In a low-NTI year, this is a meaningful earnings drag. The facility is floating-rate (SOFR-linked), adding interest rate sensitivity.

Prime brokers require minimum capital levels and their margin models may not efficiently reflect Flow Traders' portfolio. Changes in prime broker requirements, or the loss of a prime broker relationship, could constrain trading capital deployment. Net liquidity at clearing/prime brokers was €766.5m at end FY2024.

Flow Traders Strategic Capital holds digital asset and ecosystem investments that are marked to market. H1 2025 showed €4.6m of losses from the investment portfolio (included in Other income/expense). These are volatile and can create noise in reported earnings.

regulatory.description: Flow Traders operates across 180+ venues in dozens of jurisdictions and must comply with regulations in each, including MiFID II/MiFIR, MiCAR (EU digital assets), DORA (operational resilience, in force January 2025), T+1 settlement transitions, and various national market rules. Non-compliance could result in fines, license revocation, or trading suspensions.

In 2023-2024, Flow Traders received information requests from the AFM and DNB regarding compliance with the Dutch Wft and WwFT (Anti-Money Laundering Act). As of early 2025, the AFM was not proceeding with formal measures, and the DNB issued findings deemed sufficient with comments. The company committed to addressing identified shortcomings and further strengthening controls. Future scrutiny remains possible.

MiCAR is being implemented in Europe and regulatory frameworks for crypto are evolving in the US, Asia, and UK. While clearer regulation generally benefits established market makers, it may require significant compliance investment. AllUnity's EURAU stablecoin is subject to evolving e-money and stablecoin regulation in Europe.

macro.description: An extended period of suppressed market volatility across asset classes would materially reduce NTI. A benign macroeconomic environment with stable central bank policy, geopolitical calm, and low uncertainty is the single biggest macro risk for Flow Traders. FY2023 demonstrated this risk concretely: NTI fell to €300m with EBITDA margins of 23%.

Asia represented 25% of FY2025 NTI and is the primary growth engine. US-China trade tensions, potential restrictions on foreign financial firms' access to Chinese markets, and broader APAC geopolitical instability could impair Asian operations.

The company reports in EUR but has significant USD-denominated revenues (Americas) and the $200m credit facility is USD-denominated. A strengthening EUR vs. USD reduces the reported value of Americas revenues. However, the USD credit facility provides a partial natural hedge.

execution.description: CEO Mike Kuehnel stepped down in August 2025. New CEO Thomas Spitz joined September 1, 2025. While Spitz has articulated a clear growth agenda and the Board conducted an extensive search, any leadership transition introduces execution risk, particularly with a planned Capital Markets Day presentation of an ambitious new strategy expected in 2026.

Flow Traders' proprietary trading algorithms and models could malfunction, contain errors, or fail to adapt to rapidly changing market microstructure. A software bug, rogue algorithm, or technology outage could result in significant losses or reputational damage. The firm operates 24/7 across multiple asset classes, increasing operational complexity and the surface area for potential failures.

execution.risk: Digital asset and RWA strategy execution
execution.description: The company is making simultaneous bets on digital assets, tokenization (RWA via Dinari), and the AllUnity stablecoin ecosystem. These markets are nascent and high-risk. AllUnity requires regulatory approvals, adoption by financial institutions, and market infrastructure development. Failure to scale these initiatives could disappoint growth expectations and result in write-offs of strategic investments.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global ETP AuM grew 28% in 2024 to $14.8tn and reached $16.9tn by end of June 2025, with record inflows of $898bn in H1 2025. Industry consensus projects $25tn by 2030, implying continued structural growth. Fixed income ETF AuM is expected to triple from $2tn to $6tn by 2030. Digital asset investment products saw $50.77bn net inflows in 2025, bringing AuM to $172.5bn. ETP market making is a structurally growing business with strong secular tailwinds.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — Flow Traders' NTI is directly tied to trading volumes and bid-ask spreads, both positively correlated with market volatility (VIX). The business is counter-cyclical to traditional value businesses: it performs best in volatile/crisis periods (FY2020 NTI ~€697m, FY2022 NTI €472m, 4Q24 NTI €154m on elevated VIX) and poorly in calm markets (FY2023 NTI €300m). This creates its own earnings cycle uncorrelated with typical economic cycles.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low to moderate. Higher rates tend to increase fixed income market volatility and trading volumes, benefiting the FICC book. The new floating-rate private credit facility (SOFR + 5%) creates modest upside cost sensitivity to rate increases. Rate uncertainty drives volatility, which is generally positive for Flow Traders.
key_input_costs: Technology infrastructure: co-location, data feeds, hardware (€70.6m in FY2025, up 6% YoY)
Fixed employee expenses: salaries for quants, engineers, traders (€97.3m in FY2025, up 19% YoY)
Variable employee expenses: performance bonuses tied to NTI (€77.4m in FY2025)
Interest on private credit facility (SOFR + 5%, approximately €12-15m annualized from FY2026)
Exchange and trading venue fees, prime brokerage costs
macro_factors.currency_exposure: EUR-reporting with meaningful USD and HKD/CNH-denominated revenue streams. Americas revenue (~15-16% of total) is predominantly USD-denominated. Asia (~22-25%) is a mix of USD, HKD, SGD, and increasingly CNH. New $200m USD-denominated credit facility creates a partial natural hedge against USD revenue.
macro_factors.regulatory_environment: MiCAR (EU crypto regulation) provides regulatory clarity for digital asset market making in Europe — positive for Flow Traders' leading position. DORA (Digital Operational Resilience Act) in force from January 2025 requires enhanced technology resilience. T+1 settlement in the US is complete; EU T+1 transition expected to create operational changes and near-term volatility. MiFID II/MiFIR review continues to shape European market structure. Overall regulatory direction toward increased transparency and electronification favors professional market makers with established compliance infrastructure.

recent_developments.event: FY2025 full-year results released: NTI €485.8m (+4% YoY), Total Income €480.5m (flat), EBITDA €198.9m, EBITDA margin 41%, Net Profit €133.6m (-16% YoY), EPS €3.07. Trading Capital grew 35% to €1,044m. ETP value traded grew 26% to €1,940bn for FY2025. Fixed operating expenses guidance for FY2026 set at €220-230m.

Secured $200m private credit facility (SOFR+500bps, 6-year maturity, co-led by Benefit Street Partners and Stone Point Credit) plus a $75m revolving credit facility to fund the Trading Capital Expansion Plan, replacing the prior €25m bank loan. Also expanded funding facilities for Asia. Expected ~€3m interest expense in Q4 2025 alone.

Thomas Spitz assumed the role of CEO and Executive Director, replacing Mike Kuehnel. Marc Jansen simultaneously appointed Co-Chief Trading Officer and Executive Director. Spitz brings extensive global markets trading experience and has articulated plans for an ambitious growth strategy to be presented at a Capital Markets Day before the 2026 AGM.

AllUnity (Flow Traders / DWS / Galaxy joint venture) launched EURAU, Europe's first BaFin-approved MiCA-compliant EUR stablecoin, built on Ethereum and fully collateralized with reserves at multiple European banks. Flow Traders serves as designated market maker for EURAU.

Deutsche Borse Group and AllUnity signed a Memorandum of Understanding for EURAU to be made available for institutional custody through Clearstream. Subsequently, AllUnity also introduced a CHF-denominated stablecoin (CHFAU) in February 2026.
Launched active trading in China markets, described by CEO Spitz as 'an attractive growth segment aligned with our core ETP strength.' This marks a meaningful step in the Asia expansion strategy.

Strategic partnership with Dinari announced: Flow Traders to act as designated market maker for Dinari's tokenized US equities (dShares) across the Dinari Financial Network and centralized exchanges, enabling 24/7 trading of 200+ tokenized US equities with Q1 2026 launch.

Strong H1 2025 results: NTI €283.6m (+37% YoY), EBITDA margin 46.7%, Net Profit €87.5m (+48% YoY). H1 ETP value traded was a record €999bn (+32% YoY). Driven by elevated market volatility from US tariff announcements (Liberation Day). Asia NTI surged 130% YoY in H1.

Trading Capital Expansion Plan announced: dividend suspended until further notice and a €25m bank loan taken out to begin capital base expansion. The plan was the defining strategic initiative of 2024, enabling Flow Traders to deliver its second-best year in company history (FY2024 NTI €467.8m, net profit €159.5m).

items.notes: Up from FY2025 actuals of €204.1m (approximately +8-13% YoY). Driven by continued technology investments, talent additions in growth areas (Asia, digital assets, quant research), and inflationary pressures. Excludes interest on the private credit facility, which is reported separately within Interest Expenses. History of guidance: FY2025 initial guidance was €190-210m, updated to €200-205m in 3Q25, final came in at €204.1m.

First full year of the $200m private credit facility at SOFR + 5% (decreasing to SOFR + 4.5% under certain conditions). Interest expenses were €4.4m in FY2025 (approximately 2 months of the new facility). Does not include revolving credit facility if undrawn.

Management does not provide NTI or revenue guidance as it is dependent on market volatility and trading volumes, which are inherently unpredictable. CEO commentary for FY2026 was constructive on digital asset convergence, China market entry, and AI-driven trading enhancement.

Trading Capital was €1,044m at end FY2025 (up 35% YoY). The $200m private credit facility and $75m revolving credit facility provide capacity for further deployment. Return on average trading capital was 53% in FY2025.

New CEO Thomas Spitz announced a Capital Markets Day to present a comprehensive growth strategy, ambitions, and expansion plans. This is expected to be the first time the company provides medium-term quantitative targets under new leadership. Significant event for investor sentiment.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Thomas Spitz (FY2025 results, February 12, 2026): 'Following a fourth quarter marked by stronger market activity and continued growth across the global ETP ecosystem, Flow Traders delivered a solid finish to the year. Trading conditions were more constructive than in the preceding quarter, with higher ETP value traded and increased activity across several asset classes. This supported a robust EBITDA margin of 41% for both the quarter and the full year, alongside FY25 Net Profit of €133.6m and EPS of €3.07... We also broadened our footprint in Asia and have just launched our operations to begin actively trading China markets which is an attractive growth segment aligned with our core ETP strength. Momentum in the convergence between traditional finance and digital assets remains strong. 2025 was a turning point following the 2024 launches of ETPs related to cryptocurrencies... We are particularly excited about the developments of real-world asset tokenisation as it combines Flow Traders' expertise on the ETP and digital asset side. Tokenization is the new ETP moment... The energy and alignment behind our growth agenda give me great confidence as we invest into 2026.'

bull_case: Structural ETP growth tailwind is compelling: global ETP AuM is on track to reach $25tn by 2030 from $14.8tn at end-2024, with record inflows of $1.88tn in 2024. Each new product category — crypto ETPs, active ETFs, fixed income ETFs, thematic ETFs — creates incremental trading opportunities. Flow Traders' position as a top-tier liquidity provider means it benefits directly and proportionally from market growth.

Digital assets and tokenization represent a generational opportunity: Flow Traders was the #1 crypto ETP market maker in Europe in FY2024-FY2025. AllUnity's EURAU launched and was immediately onboarded by Deutsche Borse in 2025. The Dinari partnership positions Flow Traders at the forefront of 24/7 tokenized securities — a market that analysts estimate could reach $30tn by 2030. These first-mover positions in structurally large markets are difficult to value but could be transformative.

Asia is a proven multi-year growth engine with significant runway: NTI grew from €36.8m (FY2023) to €81.5m (FY2024) to €122m (FY2025) — more than 3x in two years. The recent launch of China market trading represents the next leg. Asia ETP markets remain fragmented and underpenetrated relative to Europe and the US, providing a long runway of organic growth that does not depend on winning market share from incumbents.

Exceptional operating leverage amplifies NTI upside: Fixed operating expenses are relatively stable at €204m (FY2025). In high-volatility environments the firm demonstrated NTI of €1.07bn in FY2021 on a similar cost base, implying 80%+ EBITDA margins. The FY2025 cost base is 35% higher than FY2021, but NTI capacity has grown proportionally via capital expansion. A sustained volatility uptick would deliver outsized earnings growth on the current cost structure.

Trading Capital Expansion creates compounding NTI capacity: capital grew 35% to €1,044m in FY2025 with Return on Average Trading Capital of 53% — a high-quality return on incremental capital. Each additional €100m of trading capital, deployed at historical returns, generates approximately €50m of additional NTI annually with minimal incremental fixed cost, creating a compounding value-creation mechanism as capital grows.
bear_case: Volatility dependency creates structurally unpredictable and potentially severe earnings declines: a prolonged calm market environment can compress NTI by 30-40% from normalized levels (FY2023 NTI of €300m was 65% below the FY2021 peak of €1.07bn). There is no defensive floor to earnings in such periods, no recurring revenue, and no customer contracts to rely on. Investors must price in a wide range of potential earnings outcomes.

Scale disadvantage is widening against private competitors who face no capital return obligations: Citadel Securities earned ~$9.7bn in 2024 (20x Flow Traders' NTI), Jane Street captured 10% of US equity market volume, and Optiver aggressively expanded US presence with a new Manhattan office in August 2025. These firms can invest in technology, talent, and capital with no requirement to satisfy public market shareholders. The competitive gap in resources is structural and may be difficult to bridge.

Americas market structural challenge limits full participation in the largest ETP market: the US represents 85-90% of global ETP volumes, yet Flow Traders generates only 15-16% of NTI from Americas. This is not for lack of investment — Flow Traders has been present in the US for years. The entrenched network effects and regulatory advantages of Citadel Securities and Jane Street in US equities and options appear durable, and Flow Traders' inability to crack this market meaningfully constrains total addressable NTI.

Dividend suspension with no resumption timeline and new financial leverage reduces shareholder returns in the near term: shareholders who bought expecting income must now accept that capital is being retained and levered up for growth with no guaranteed return. If the Trading Capital Expansion Plan does not generate NTI growth sufficient to compensate for foregone dividends and new interest costs (~€12-15m/year), the capital allocation decision will have destroyed shareholder value in the short-to-medium term.

Simultaneous execution risk across multiple strategic initiatives: new CEO (Spitz, September 2025), new leverage ($200m credit facility), China market entry (H2 2025), AllUnity EUR stablecoin scaling, Dinari tokenized equity launch (Q1 2026), and a deep learning trading initiative are all happening simultaneously. Spreading management attention and capital across all these initiatives increases the probability of underexecution on any one of them. The planned Capital Markets Day will test whether management can articulate a credible, focused roadmap.
